title: Oy Chanukah
description: The Yiddish Hanukkah song as Susman Kisselgof's school songbook printed it, a lively Hasidic dance tune for 2 to 4 singers, sung in Yiddish (the words are shown in Latin letters): the soprano and alto sing Pesach Lvov's two printed voices, the tenor joins on the words and the bass bounces underneath on "dm". The first verse is about the holiday's fun: spinning dreidels, hot latkes, lighting the little candles and dancing; the second praises Judah the Maccabee, who drove out the enemy and brought Jerusalem back to life. Quick and light, with many short syllables.

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on Pesach Lvov's two voices and piano part, as revised for the second edition (1914) under A. Zhitomirsky (died 1937) (public domain: Lvov died 22 February 1913, as the book's memorial page and the Jewish Encyclopedia of Russia give it): the soprano and alto are his voices as printed, the tenor and bass are taken from his piano's left hand
licence.source: tune, words and harmony from Susman Kisselgof, Lider-zamelbukh far der yidisher shul un familye (first edition St Petersburg, 1911/12; read from the fourth edition, Berlin: Yuval, 192-?), No. 24, "Oj chanuke, oj chanuke. A chanuke lid. (Chsidisch.) Werter fun M. Riwesman. Arrangirt fun P. Lwow.", p. 32, in F minor in 2/4, Allegretto, M.M. 88 to the quarter, "Freilich", Meno mosso from bar 9, sopranos and altos with piano, kept here in F minor at 80; the first verse under the notes, both verses in Yiddish letters in the words section, p. 13 (No. 24), checked against the 1912 words booklet; read from the scans at archive.org/details/nybc202667 (leaves n142 and n16). Kisselgof died 1939, Rivesman 1924, Lvov 1913. The Yiddish is transliterated from the print in YIVO-style romanization, in standard YIVO spelling; in verse 2 a few notes are split on the same pitch for its extra syllables
